Let <MATH_0001> be an algebraic stack. The following are equivalent
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0002> is reduced and <MATH_0003> is a singleton,
<STRUCT_0003> there exists a surjective flat morphism <MATH_0004>
where <MATH_0005> is a field, and
<STRUCT_0004> there exists a locally of finite type, surjective, flat morphism
<MATH_0006> where <MATH_0007> is a field.
<STRUCT_0005>

Assume (1). Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme and
let <MATH_0002> be a surjective smooth morphism. Then <MATH_0003> is
a reduced scheme. Let <MATH_0004> be a generic point of an irreducible
component of <MATH_0005>. Since <MATH_0006> is reduced we have
<MATH_0007>. It follows that the canonical
morphism <MATH_0008> is flat. We see that the
composition <MATH_0009> is flat (see
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma <REF_0001>).
It is also surjective as <MATH_0010> is a singleton. In other words
(2) holds.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Assume (2). Let <MATH_0011> be a scheme and
let <MATH_0012> be a surjective smooth morphism. Choose a field
<MATH_0013> and a surjective flat morphism <MATH_0014>.
Then <MATH_0015> is an algebraic space smooth
over <MATH_0016>, hence regular (see
Spaces over Fields, Lemma <REF_0002>)
and in particular reduced. Since <MATH_0017>
is surjective and flat we conclude that <MATH_0018> is reduced
(Descent on Spaces, Lemma <REF_0003>).
In other words (1) holds.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
It is clear that (3) implies (2). Finally, assume (2). Pick a nonempty
affine scheme <MATH_0019> and a smooth morphism <MATH_0020>. Pick a closed
point <MATH_0021> and set <MATH_0022>. The composition
<MATH_0023>
is locally of finite type by
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemmas
<REF_0004> and
<REF_0005>.
It is also flat and surjective by
Lemma <REF_0006>.
Hence (3) holds.
